editorial:
Imagine waking up to find out your father, a world-famous psychologist who spent his whole life helping people survive their darkest days, has suddenly died by suicide. That is exactly what happens to the teenage daughter in this mystery. She knows her dad too well to believe he would give up on life, so she decides to play detective. She teams up with one of his old patients to dig into his secret files and figure out who actually killed him. It feels like a classic whodunit where you are constantly questioning who is telling the truth and who is hiding something.

What really makes this work is the slow build-up and the surprising reveal at the end. The acting is solid, and the 1960s London setting adds a nice touch of style. While some parts might feel a bit slow if you are used to modern action movies, the payoff is totally worth it. If you enjoy a good puzzle, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The big twist is that the father did not kill himself or get murdered by a stranger. He actually died because of a secret experiment he was running on himself to understand the human mind. He pushed himself too far and suffered a mental break that led to his death. The daughter finds out that her father was not the perfect man she thought he was, making the ending both sad and shocking.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school mysteries and psychological puzzles.
